clue.text: Built, as ordered, around new city in Turkey

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are wrapped around the next piece
the letters are put in a new order, so the words before it are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a famous Turkish city was built to plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as ordered' looks like one phrase, but 'as' is part of the shuffled letters, giving ISTABUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is the largest metropolis of Turkey, straddling Europe and Asia.

clue.text: One may be running starkers, briefly, around middle of field

definitions.text: One may be running starkers, briefly, around middle of field

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the centre letter of field
running can mean in disorder, so the letters that follow are rearranged
cut short: the last letter of the word starkers is dropped
the central letter of the word field is taken

explanation.surface: A naked pitch invader dashes about a sports field, and the whole clue describes him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims STARKERS to STARKER, 'running' rearranges it to STRAKER, and 'around' puts E (middle of 'field') inside it. Read whole, the clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A streaker is someone who dashes naked through a public place, classically across a sports pitch.

clue.text: Fleet, American — not all there captured by artist

indicators.note: the artist's letters close round the madness, holding it captive

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
someone not all there is mad

explanation.surface: An American who is a bit unhinged is caught by a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Miner clipped dog

indicators.note: clipped means cut short, so the final letter of the miner word goes

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: A miner's hound has been given a trim.
explanation.definitionFit: The collie is a Scottish sheepdog breed, such as the Border collie.

clue.text: Gloomy beggar at the end with nothing in hat

parts.note: sombre means dark and gloomy

indicators.note: only the final letter of beggar is used

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A sad beggar sits at the end of the street with nothing in his hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Live it up, taking in a show

indicators.note: the revel word takes the A inside it

parts.note: to revel is to celebrate and live it up

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a night out, catching a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to show or disclose it; both are verbs.

clue.text: Small milliner greatly upset

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a hatter, like a milliner, makes hats

explanation.surface: A little hat-maker is terribly distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter someone is to devastate them emotionally, as in 'shattered by the news'.

clue.text: A wild urge to quarrel

indicators.note: wild suggests something out of control, so the word urge is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has an uncontrollable impulse to pick a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to dispute heatedly, which is to quarrel.

clue.text: Couple in book holding pig back

indicators.note: the book word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: back tells us to read the pig word in reverse

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A pair of lovers features in a novel that carries a pig on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads like the pig being carried, but it signals reading the pig word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a pair of people, a couple.

clue.text: Path, mostly to right, will find tower?

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the last letter of the path word is dropped

parts.note: a track is a path
taken as written

explanation.surface: Directions: follow the path, keep right, and you will reach a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TRACK to TRAC. 'tower' is not a tall building here but something that tows, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is a vehicle often used to tow trailers and ploughs, so it is a tower.

clue.text: Early invader's point of view

definitions.meaning: one of the Germanic people who invaded Britain in the fifth century; the 's is 'is'
a standpoint or way of seeing things

explanation.surface: A historian describes the perspective of an ancient invader.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles gave England its name; an angle is also a viewpoint or slant on a story.

clue.text: A bishop housed in a villa, in resort close to diocese, for free

indicators.note: the bishop's letter is lodged inside the rearranged letters
read as re-sort: the letters of a villa are sorted again into a new order

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

indicators.note: the close, or last letter, of diocese

explanation.surface: A bishop is staying in a villa at a resort near his diocese, without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in resort' rearranges A VILLA to VAILAL; 'housed in' puts B inside to give VAILABL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available is free to be had or used, unoccupied.

clue.text: Starter of bran flakes a caterer put out in a dish first thing?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of bran is taken
put out suggests disturbed, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A caterer serves bran flakes in a bowl as a morning starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges FLAKES A CATERER to REAKFASTCEREAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast cereal is a dish such as cornflakes eaten in the morning, hence first thing in the day.

clue.text: Sucker beat target!

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
prey is a hunter's target

explanation.surface: An exclamation: a dupe has been thrashed and made a victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' suggests a gullible person, but it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamprey is an eel-like fish that clings to prey with a sucking mouth.

clue.text: Austen heroine crossing over heath

indicators.note: the heroine's surname straddles, or goes across, the other letter

parts.note: Catherine Morland is the heroine of Jane Austen's Northanger Abbey
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A Jane Austen heroine walks across the heath.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorland is open uncultivated upland, the same kind of ground as a heath.

clue.text: Surrendered and brought in

definitions.meaning: an investment that ... money brought it in as return

explanation.surface: Someone gave up and was taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is both to give in and to produce a return, as a crop or an investment does.

clue.text: Kid attending party left large plaything

parts.note: to rag is to tease or kid
a do is a party
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A child goes to a party and leaves a big toy behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' is the verb, to tease, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag doll is a soft stuffed toy made of cloth, a child's plaything.

clue.text: Apache chief in rocky region north of Missouri

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits above the second
rocky means unsteady, so the word region is rearranged

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Missouri

explanation.surface: An Apache leader lives in mountainous country above Missouri.
explanation.definitionFit: Geronimo was the famous leader of the Apache people who resisted US forces.

clue.text: Fortune duly affected during shortage

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go within the shortage word

parts.note: a lack is a shortage

indicators.note: affected means changed, so the word duly is rearranged

explanation.surface: Wealth is duly hit in a time of scarcity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges the letters to DYLU before they go inside. 'Fortune' looks like wealth but is chance personified.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Luck is chance personified, the goddess Fortune.

clue.text: Labour in vain in one's stocking feet?

definitions.meaning: ... is a pointless mission, bootless meaning useless
read literally, someone in stocking feet is without boots

explanation.surface: Someone works for nothing while wearing only socks.
explanation.walkthrough: Bootless is an old word for useless; the question mark flags the jokey literal reading of shoeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A bootless errand is a fruitless task, an old phrase from Shakespeare.

clue.text: Woman who wrote about four sisters inhabiting rural cottage

definitions.text: Woman who wrote about four sisters

indicators.note: the answer lives inside the run of letters in the words rural cottage

explanation.surface: A writer of a novel about four sisters lives in a country cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott wrote Little Women, about the four March sisters.

clue.text: Last to comment on old Pope's headdress

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the second
only the final letter of comment is taken

parts.note: Urban was the name of eight popes, the last in the 1600s

explanation.surface: A final remark on the headgear of a historic pontiff.
explanation.definitionFit: A turban is a head covering of long cloth wound round the head.

clue.text: Watch cutter swing

parts.note: to see is to watch
a saw is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: Someone observes a woodsman swinging a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to swing up and down or back and forth.

clue.text: Trembling poplar in Anglo-Saxon enclosure

parts.note: a pen is an animal enclosure

explanation.surface: A shivering tree grows inside an old English field boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar whose leaves quiver in the slightest breeze, hence 'trembling'.

clue.text: Poet could be godlier, somehow, in church

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are put inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of godlier are worked into a different order

explanation.surface: A poet might become more devout in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal turns GODLIER into OLERIDG. 'Poet could be godlier' reads as a statement about piety, hiding that 'could be' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Taylor Coleridge was the Romantic poet of The Rime of the Ancient Mariner.

clue.text: Writer retired by a lake in a Himalayan country

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the writer word is read backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An author has retired beside a lake in a mountain kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns PEN to NEP. 'Writer' looks like an author but is the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a landlocked country lying in the Himalayas, home to Everest.

clue.text: Drank a rum after initially taking pot

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the initial letter
only the first letter of taking is used
rum means odd or strange, so the letters of drank are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone downed a rum after first smoking some weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is not the drink but an anagram signal, turning DRANK into NKARD. 'pot' is not cannabis but a drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large drinking mug, often pewter, a pot for beer.

clue.text: Yearbook hidden by naval man, a commodore

indicators.note: the answer lies concealed across the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: A naval officer keeps an annual record out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual publication of calendars, tides and data, a yearbook.
